findings.title: MCP stdio env denylist missing GCONV_PATH / PERL5OPT / PERL5LIB / RUBYOPT / RUBYLIB loader-injection keys

tracking.upstream_pr: DENIED (fork-scoped App); open manually via compare_url

findings.notes: DANGEROUS_MCP_ENV_KEYS backstop for the mcp_stdio_command_allowlist listed PATH/LD_PRELOAD/LD_AUDIT/DYLD_*/PYTHON*/NODE_OPTIONS/NODE_PATH/BASH_ENV/ENV but omitted same-class loader/interpreter code-injection vars. GCONV_PATH (glibc loads attacker .so on next iconv, hits ANY glibc binary like LD_PRELOAD, not just interpreters) and PERL5OPT/PERL5LIB, RUBYOPT/RUBYLIB (Perl/Ruby analogues of PYTHONPATH/NODE_OPTIONS) passed reject_dangerous_env_keys and merged into the spawned MCP server env, so a config pinning command to a trusted wrapper could still inject code. Defense-in-depth (low sev): only relevant when an admin has configured mcp_stdio_command_allowlist; prerequisites (attacker file on disk + matching wrapper) identical to the already-listed LD_PRELOAD/PYTHONPATH entries. Fix: added the 5 keys to the frozenset + parametrized test in tests/test_mcp_policy.py, based on upstream d9f76a5, authored as Herik Webb, single commit 'fix(mcp): deny GCONV_PATH and perl/ruby loader keys in stdio env denylist'. Logic verified directly (module loaded standalone; new keys rejected incl. case/whitespace forms; safe keys + existing entries unaffected; full pytest not run - env lacks tiktoken/optional deps). Pushed to fork origin. Cross-fork PR into upstream DENIED (session GitHub scope fork-only) -> open manually via compare_url. Fork-only-file guard passed; git log author verified Herik Webb. Found via 4-surface parallel Pass B review; only validated non-duplicate finding this run.

findings.title: search_files / list_files (nbi-file-read toolset) glob `pattern` argument is not containment-checked, so a `..`-bearing pattern escapes jupyter_root_dir -> arbitrary workspace-external file read/enumeration
findings.attacker_model: Indirect prompt injection: untrusted content the user asks Claude/NBI to work with (malicious notebook cell/data file, README in a cloned repo, third-party GitHub skill body, or an MCP tool result) steers the LLM into calling the FileRead tools with a crafted `pattern`. Attacker is NOT the user.
findings.attack_path: Both tools sandbox only the `directory` arg via safe_jupyter_path, then pass the LLM-supplied `pattern` straight into search_dir.glob(pattern); Path.glob honors `..` segments and follows symlinks, yielding paths outside the root. search_files then does `except ValueError: rel_path = file_path` and still open()s and returns the contents; list_files enumerates them. content_pattern='.' matches every line -> full arbitrary read. read_file is NOT affected (routes its path through safe_jupyter_path).
findings.impact: Complete bypass of the workspace sandbox these tools advertise: read SSH keys, ~/.aws/credentials, /etc/passwd, and — on a shared JupyterHub node — other tenants' files, bounded only by the server process's own permissions. Results flow back into the chat/LLM (exfiltration channel).
findings.evidence: Reproduced on Python 3.11.15: root.glob('../creds/aws') returns the outside file; search_files(pattern='../creds/aws', content_pattern='.') returned the outside file's line contents; list_files(pattern='../creds/*') enumerated the outside dir; a workspace-internal symlink to /etc/hostname was also read. search_files L343 (except ValueError: rel_path=file_path) + L346 open(); list_files L440/L443 glob.
findings.fix: Filter every glob hit through the existing containment chokepoint before use: keep only matches for which safe_jupyter_path(str(f)) succeeds (it resolves `..` and symlinks then checks relative_to(root)). Closes the `..` vector and the symlink variant together; prepared as a 33/-2 patch to built_in_toolsets.py, verified to block traversal while preserving legitimate in-workspace globbing.
findings.disclosure: Held for PRIVATE disclosure per upstream plmbr/notebook-intelligence SECURITY.md ('Do not open a public GitHub issue... Email mbektasgh@outlook.com'). No public PR/issue opened; fork auto-promotion pipeline deliberately not triggered. Finding + patch surfaced privately to the routine owner (herikwebb) to relay to the maintainer. nbi-file-read is explicitly in upstream's in-scope list.
findings.related: Same functions/root-cause as the two recorded symlink findings ('search_files symlink traversal' fixed_upstream; 'list_files enumerates host files through workspace symlinks' active); this `..`-in-pattern vector is a distinct, previously-unrecorded attack path and the proposed fix resolves all three.
findings.update_2026_07_18: Re-verified at upstream tip 395cba7 (v5.3.0-a1). search_files HALF is now FIXED upstream in v5.3.0-a1: it rejects escaping patterns via _glob_pattern_escapes and enumerates via the sandbox-aware _iter_pattern_matches, gating each match through safe_jupyter_path -- the arbitrary CONTENT-read vector is closed. The list_files HALF is STILL LIVE: list_files() still calls list_dir.glob(pattern) with the LLM-supplied pattern, with no _glob_pattern_escapes check and no per-match safe_jupyter_path gate, and on relative_to() failure sets item_relpath=item (the outside path) and still lists it. Reproduced end-to-end on Python 3.11.15 at 395cba7: pattern='../secret/*' lists ../secret/aws_creds; '../*' enumerates the parent; 'linky/*' follows an in-workspace symlink to an outside dir; '/etc/hostname' confirms existence. Remaining exposure is ENUMERATION / existence+path disclosure only (list, not content read), i.e. effective severity MEDIUM now that the content-read half is fixed. Minimal fix prepared on fork branch security/fix-list-files-glob-escape-20260718121118-11796 (branched off upstream/main 395cba7): adds the same two gates search_files uses to list_files (+ a parallel list_files sandbox test suite); 149 insertions across built_in_toolsets.py and tests/test_builtin_list_files_sandbox.py. Fix + all 6 test scenarios verified against the actual patched code standalone (project pytest suite not runnable in this container: Debian PyJWT + tiktoken import-time network fetch).
